chunks: And in the narration of Mu‘āwiyah ibn Wahb, he said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at what age a child is to be held to fasting.
He عليه السلام said: 'Between fourteen and fifteen years. If he fasts before that, then leave him be. My son so-and-so fasted before that, and I left him.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: fourteen years of age, mentioned as the lower point of the range
key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: a young boy or child who has not yet reached full legal accountability
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting), the act of abstaining as an obligation in Islam
key_terms.خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: fifteen years of age, mentioned as the upper point of the range
key_terms.فَدَعْهُ: leave him; allow him to continue without preventing him

ai.seo_question: At what age is a child required to begin fasting according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the age at which a child is taken to be accountable for sawm (fasting), indicating an age range between fourteen and fifteen years. It also shows that if a child fasts before that age voluntarily, he should be allowed to continue. The narration reflects a practical legal ruling alongside a familial example from the Imam عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1906 - In the narration of Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, he said:
"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) at what age a child should be required to fast.
Imam (as) said: 'Between fourteen and fifteen years of age. If he fasts before that, let him be. My son so-and-so fasted before that age, and I left him to it.'"
